answer: Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short. The haven of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. The nectar holds work receipts rather than names, so the mirror of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. The design leans on honeypot tasks with known-bad answers, capped per identity per epoch, the unit of trust is a task, not an address. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work.
